title: Eligibility for the Resilience Fund is proven by onchain participation history, not by identity documents
content:
A.2.9.1.1.1.4.1.1 makes an Ethereum address the credential: an applicant "must first select an Ethereum address that is linked to their activity at Sky (\"Proof of Eligibility\" or \"POE\")." Valid PoEs are all behavioural histories — being an owner signing from a Sky multisig; having "voted directly or through delegation in at least ten Governance Polls or Executive Votes"; a compensation history (six payouts over six months, or an equivalent vesting stream); or holding above a token threshold. The applicant signs an application message from that address (A.2.9.1.1.1.4.1.3).

The design achievement is that a legal-defense programme is gated without identity verification. Contribution is verifiable and durable onchain, so the fund can distinguish a genuine participant from an opportunist while remaining compatible with the pseudonymity that Aligned Delegates and many contributors rely on.

Verification runs through governance provenance rather than a database: A.2.9.1.1.1.4.1.6 requires the Committee member to "identify this governance decision by verifying the Spell that enacted the Executive Vote," since "[t]his Spell contains the hash of the respective Executive Vote." Eligibility is thus traced to an immutable execution record.

The residual gap is handled socially. Where no PoE exists, "a verified Beneficiary must attest eligibility on behalf of the applicant," assessed case by case — a web-of-trust fallback that reintroduces exactly the subjectivity the onchain proofs were meant to eliminate, and does so for the applicants hardest to evaluate.
description: Applicants nominate an Ethereum address and qualify via multisig signing, ten or more votes, a payment history, or a token threshold — with peer attestation as the fallback when none exists.
